properties.statement:
TWO DEFECTS FIXED 2026-08-23 FROM ONE FEEDBACK READ, AND THEY ARE THE SAME DEFECT. Both told a caller something reassuring that was false, and neither could have been found by anyone who believed the tool.

① THE SNAPSHOT WARNING WAS FALSE AND ITS REMEDY WOULD HAVE CAUSED THE LOSS IT WARNED ABOUT.
`snapshot_preserving` compared the WHOLE node's content hash against every snapshot. So after the ordinary sequence — record_change, write field A, write field B — nothing hashed to the state B replaced, and the revision block said "NO SNAPSHOT HOLDS THE STATE IT REPLACED — checked, not assumed" about a value sitting in the snapshot verbatim. It then prescribed a three-step undo: write the prior value back, record_change, re-apply. **A session that believed it would have snapshotted a RECONSTRUCTION over a timeline that was already correct.**
  🛑 THE PHRASE "checked, not assumed" IS WHAT MAKES IT DANGEROUS. It was added to earn trust and it succeeded; the check behind it was answering a coarser question than the sentence claimed. A message that says it looked must have looked at the thing it names.
  FIXED at the root: `prior_state_coverage` answers whole-node AND field-by-field, and the strong warning now fires only on fields nothing holds — naming them, and explicitly excluding preserved ones from the undo, because applying the undo to a preserved field IS the corruption.

② THE DURABILITY AID WAS WRITTEN, TESTED, AND FILTERED OUT OF EVERYTHING SERVED.
`loop_status.sync` reported `state: in_step` beside `export_nodes: 2897, live_nodes: 2899`. The sentence explaining that — *"2 node(s) here have never been exported… export before you finish"* — ALREADY EXISTED in `SyncDebt::message`, on the in-step line, with a comment saying it was placed there "because that is the line a session reads before standing down". It reached nobody: `loop_status` surfaces `message()` only for `is_actionable()` debts, and `in_step` is not actionable.
  ⭐ SO THE FIX WAS NOT TO WRITE ANYTHING. It was to stop discarding what was already written. The first attempt at this fix ADDED A SECOND SENTENCE saying the same thing, which was reverted on finding the original.
  🛑 AND THE VERDICT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. The obvious fix — derive `state` from the counts so `in_step` cannot appear beside `live > export` — would break `ver:the-record-moved-is-surfaced`, which pins "ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported" because `state` answers whether the RECORD moved ahead of this seat, not whether your work is durable. Changing it would fire on nearly every session mid-flight. **What was missing was never a different verdict; it was that the verdict could be read ALONE.**

⭐⭐ THE COMMON SHAPE, AND IT IS THE REASON THESE ARE ONE NODE. A tool that is wrong in the ALARMING direction gets investigated within minutes — somebody chases the alarm. A tool that is wrong in the REASSURING direction is believed, and the cost lands later on somebody who never saw the reading. Both of these were found by a reporter who refused the reassurance and paid for a control: one read the snapshot back by hand, the other re-exported and got `wrote: "changed"` against a green verdict. **Neither is reachable from inside the system, because from inside both look exactly like working.**

⚠️ AND REFLOW2 HAD ALREADY SHIPPED THE COUNTS FOR ② IN AUGUST, specifically to make the green falsifiable. They did make it falsifiable. They did not make it falsified — the reporter's words are the finding: *"`state` is the field a session reads, and the counts are the field it skims."* Adding evidence beside a verdict does not change what a reader takes away; the verdict has to carry it.
